name: IsoDAR
summary: IsoDAR is developing an intense electron-antineutrino source for an underground liquid-scintillator detector at Yemilab in South Korea. Its cyclotron and isotope-production target provide a controlled source for short-baseline oscillation and precision-interaction studies.
physics_targets: Short-baseline electron-antineutrino disappearance and sterile-neutrino tests
detection_principle: A cyclotron accelerates molecular hydrogen ions, which are stripped into protons and directed onto a beryllium target. Produced neutrons are captured in an enriched lithium-7 sleeve, creating beta-decaying lithium-8. The emitted electron antineutrinos are measured primarily through prompt-positron and delayed-neutron inverse beta decay.

status.label: Under construction
status.evidence: The collaboration website states that construction at Yemilab is underway. The 2025 source design is a preliminary design report; an operating neutrino exposure is not established.

timeline.event: Beam-transport, source and shielding preliminary design report released.

key_parameters.name: Five-year source projection
key_parameters.value: Approximately 1.15 x 10^23 electron antineutrinos in five calendar years at the design exposure
